title.en: Pensées: The Two Kinds of Mind, and the Thinking Reed
title.zh: 思想录：两种精神，和会思想的芦苇

year_display.zh: 写于 17 世纪 50 年代；1670 年出版；1904 年英译

edition.en: Seven fragments, numbered as in Léon Brunschvicg’s edition of the Pensées (first published 1897; Trotter names its twelfth edition, 1900, as his text): 1, 144, 205, 206, 346, 347 and 348. W. F. Trotter’s translation was first published in the Temple Classics (London: J. M. Dent, 1904); the text is Project Gutenberg eBook 18269, taken from a 1958 reprint, collated word for word with a scan of the 1904 edition, whose readings are restored in five places (three in 144, two in 347). T. S. Eliot’s introduction to the later reprint is not included.
edition.zh: 选七则，编号依莱昂·布伦士维格编订的《思想录》（1897 年初版；特罗特说明他所据的是 1900 年第十二版），特罗特的译本即依此编排：第 1、144、205、206、346、347、348 则。W. F. 特罗特的译本 1904 年首次收入“神殿经典丛书”（伦敦：J. M. 登特出版社）；文本取自古登堡计划电子书第 18269 号（据 1958 年的重印本），并与 1904 年版的扫描本逐字对校，有五处恢复了 1904 年版的读法（第 144 则三处，第 347 则两处）。后来重印本中 T. S. 艾略特的导言不收。

basis.en: Written in the 1650s and published in 1670; Blaise Pascal died in 1662. W. F. Trotter, the translator, died in 1945; his translation was first published in 1904.
basis.zh: 写于 17 世纪 50 年代，1670 年出版；帕斯卡卒于 1662 年。译者 W. F. 特罗特卒于 1945 年，其译本 1904 年初版。

note.en: Pascal, who had invented a calculating machine and argued about the vacuum, left these notes unfinished when he died at thirty-nine; they were meant for a defence of Christianity and were published in 1670. This selection keeps the pages about thinking itself: the mind that reasons from clear principles and the mind that sees many fine ones at a glance, the study of man that so few attempt, and the reed that knows it can be crushed. The Chinese is a complete translation of the seven fragments.
note.zh: 帕斯卡发明过计算机器，也就真空问题与人争论过；他三十九岁去世时，这些札记还没有完成。它们原是为一部为基督教辩护的书所写的，1670 年出版。这里选的是关于思想本身的几页：从清楚的原理出发推理的心智，与一眼看出许多细微原理的心智；很少有人去做的对人的研究；以及那根知道自己会被压碎的芦苇。中文为这七则的全译。

excerpt.orig: Man is but a reed, the most feeble thing in nature; but he is a thinking reed.
excerpt.en: Man is but a reed, the most feeble thing in nature; but he is a thinking reed.
excerpt.zh: 人只不过是一根芦苇，是自然界中最脆弱的东西；但他是一根会思想的芦苇。

gloss.at: The difference between the mathematical and the intuitive mind.
gloss.en: Pascal’s esprit de géométrie and esprit de finesse: the mind that reasons from a few clear principles, and the mind that takes in many subtle ones at once.
gloss.zh: 帕斯卡所说的“几何精神”与“敏感精神”：前者从少数清楚的原理出发推理，后者能一下子把握许多细微的原理。

gloss.at: the study of the abstract sciences
gloss.en: Pascal’s own work in geometry, arithmetic and physics: conic sections, the arithmetical triangle, probability and the experiments on the vacuum.
gloss.zh: 指帕斯卡本人在几何、算术和物理上的工作：圆锥曲线、算术三角形、概率，以及关于真空的实验。

gloss.en: “The remembrance of a guest who stays but one day”: from the Latin Bible, Wisdom of Solomon 5:15.
gloss.zh: “只住一日的过客的回忆”，语出拉丁文《圣经·所罗门智训》第五章第十五节。
